reflections.title: Restored and Kept by God

reflect.text: When we wander from God, our fellowship with Him is broken, but our place as His children stays secure. God does not make us wait when we repent, which means turning back to Him from our sins. He forgives and washes us clean right away, bringing back the joy of our close walk with Him and putting us back into His service.

When we leave behind what is worthless and hold to what is noble, God honors us by letting us speak His truth. Standing firm in God's truth can bring opposition from the world. Yet God promises to make us like a solid wall of bronze. People may fight against us, but they cannot win, because the Lord Himself stands with us.

In our trials, God does not ask us to rely on our own strength or look to other people for rescue. He personally promises that He will deliver and redeem us. As Charles Spurgeon wrote, "Jehovah has power enough without borrowing from our puny arm." Because the Lord is on our side, we do not need to fear the threats of the wicked.

questions: Is there any worthless habit or attitude you need to leave behind so God can renew your walk with Him?
How does knowing that God is with you give you courage to stand firm when others oppose your faith?
reflections.prayer: Lord, thank You for welcoming us back whenever we stumble, and for washing us clean with Your grace. Help us to leave behind worthless things and speak Your truth with boldness. When others oppose us, remind us that You are our bronze wall and our deliverer. Amen.

D5.author: Rick Warren
D5.work: God Can Restore You After You Sin
